specStatusNote: This file is the structured source for docs/omniverse-kit-companion.md and its generated reference appendix docs/omniverse-kit-companion-reference.g.md. It specifies a separately owned and separately distributed Omniverse Kit extension that no repository has implemented yet. Nothing here is evidence of an implementation, a publication, or an authorized Kit/Nucleus baseline: eng/omniverse-profile.json's kit-baseline dependency and the excluded-unreachable/kit-extension-companion-repo entry in eng/support-manifest.json are unchanged by this specification and remain the authoritative claims about what is and is not implemented.

kitBaseline.note: The extension.toml example's Kit baseline placeholder must resolve to this dependency's version field, not to a hardcoded number. eng/omniverse-profile.json currently declares it 'external-optional' with version 'pending' and versionSource null. It stays 'pending' until a named Kit release is independently authorized and pinned with its own repository-relative provenance file, at which point this note -- and only this note, never the placeholder text baked into an example -- is what changes.

owns: The openusd.bridge.v1 wire contract (wire.proto, service.proto) and its FileDescriptorSet
The C# gRPC client adapter (OpenUsd.Bridge.Grpc) and the LiveAuthoringSessionCoordinator semantics it drives
This specification, its machine-readable facts, and its checked pseudocode examples
Protocol compatibility tests that a companion implementation can run against, once one exists

Nucleus authentication, SSO, and token handling
Live session create/join/leave and .live layer I/O
Kit stage notices and translating them into wire updates
Every credential presented to Nucleus or to this protocol's own optional auth layer
The server side of the openusd.bridge.v1 contract: Negotiate, GetSnapshot, GetStatus, PublishLocalBatch, StreamChanges

repositoryBoundary.boundaryStatement: The wire contract is the only coupling point between the two repositories. This repository never depends on omni.client, Kit headers, or any NVIDIA-licensed source, and the companion extension never vendors this repository's source -- it depends on the published OpenUsd.Bridge.Protocol/OpenUsd.Bridge.Grpc packages (for a .NET-hosted companion) or generates Python stubs from the shipped .proto files (for a Kit-hosted companion), by version, like any other consumer. That separation is what keeps the two sides on independent release cadences and independent licenses, matching docs/omniverse-bridge.md's existing ownership table.

extensionManifestDependencies.purpose: GUI mode window, menu, and status-bar host for the companion's optional GUI extension
Kit-side stage access, stage notices, and .live layer authoring
omni:// URI resolution and Nucleus connectivity
Running the bidirectional gRPC stream loop on Kit's async event loop instead of blocking it
Generated Python protobuf/gRPC bindings produced from this repository's shipped .proto files at the companion's own build time; not a PyPI package this repository publishes

steps: Obtain the exact .proto files from the OpenUsd.Bridge.Protocol package version the companion targets: src/OpenUsd.Bridge.Protocol/protos/openusd/bridge/v1/wire.proto and service.proto, or the equivalent FileDescriptorSet returned by OpenUsd.Bridge.Protocol.BridgeProtocol.CreateDescriptorSet() for a descriptor-driven toolchain that does not have file system access to the .proto sources.

Generate stubs with grpcio-tools: python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I<protos-root> --python_out=<gen> --grpc_python_out=<gen> --pyi_out=<gen> openusd/bridge/v1/wire.proto openusd/bridge/v1/service.proto. Pin grpcio, grpcio-tools, and protobuf to versions compatible with the companion's own Kit Python runtime, not to whatever this repository's own tests happen to use.

Never hand-edit generated _pb2.py/_pb2_grpc.py output. Regenerate it whenever the companion's pinned OpenUsd.Bridge.Protocol package version changes, and record which package version the checked-in (or build-time-generated) stubs were produced from.

Verify the generated stub's package/version against the running server by reading openusd.bridge.v1.ProtocolVersion off the negotiated HandshakeResponse at connect time, never by trusting the generator invocation alone: a stale generated stub and a live server can disagree even when both files were technically regenerated.

Package/version negotiation happens at the application layer (Negotiate), not at the gRPC/protobuf layer: a major-version mismatch is rejected by BridgeNegotiator-equivalent logic on both sides before any mutating call, and a newer minor version only adds capabilities.

Configure the generated stub's channel with the same message-size, TLS, and keepalive options documented in maxMessageOptions and docs/omniverse-bridge.md's Security table so a Python server enforces the identical bounds the C# client already assumes.
pythonGrpcWorkflow.packageNegotiation: The companion never assumes its generated stub's package name or version matches the peer. It reads openusd.bridge.v1.PackageName ('openusd.bridge.v1') from the descriptor and openusd.bridge.v1.ProtocolVersion.{major,minor} from the negotiated HandshakeResponse, and refuses to proceed past Negotiate when the major version differs, exactly like the C# BridgeNegotiator.

maxMessageOptions.grpcMaxSendMessageLength: BridgeProtocol.MaxFrameBytes (MaxEstimatedBatchPayloadBytes + 65536), passed as grpc.max_send_message_length on both the Python server and any Python client
maxMessageOptions.grpcMaxReceiveMessageLength: BridgeProtocol.MaxFrameBytes (MaxEstimatedBatchPayloadBytes + 65536), passed as grpc.max_receive_message_length; a frame at exactly the negotiated effective limit must still fit, so this bound is never set to the negotiated effective limit alone

preconditions: No prior successful Negotiate on this connection/session attempt
steps: Reject immediately, with HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_UNAUTHENTICATED, when the presented credential (if any auth layer is configured) does not validate; never distinguish 'missing' from 'invalid' in the detail text
Check request.client_version.major against the server's own major version; reject with HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_VERSION on any mismatch before evaluating capabilities or limits

Compute agreed capabilities as the intersection of request.client_capabilities and the server's supported capabilities; reject with HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_CAPABILITY when CAPABILITY_FULL_SNAPSHOT or CAPABILITY_ORDERED_DELTA is missing from that intersection
Compute effective_limits as the element-wise minimum of request.client_limits and the server's own enforced limits; reject with HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_LIMITS when any resulting bound is non-positive

Verify request.bridge_root_path equals the one absolute prim path this server instance owns for the requesting Nucleus session/stage; reject with HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_BRIDGE_ROOT on any other value, including a sub-path or a parent path

When request.requested_session_id is present and still live on this server, resume that session's existing epoch unchanged; otherwise mint a new SessionEpoch (fresh session_id, epoch = 0 unless a prior epoch for the same remote_origin_id is being retired, in which case epoch increments)
Return accepted = true with server_version, the agreed capabilities, effective_limits, the resolved epoch, and bridge_root_path echoed back exactly; never return accepted = true without an epoch
Never transparently retry a Negotiate call at the transport layer even though it looks read-only: it establishes a session and an epoch, so a retried call could mint a second session

preconditions: A prior successful Negotiate on this session
steps: Validate request.epoch.session_id and .epoch match exactly the session and epoch this connection negotiated; on any mismatch -- stale (older) or advanced (newer) -- fail the call instead of substituting a snapshot for a different epoch. A snapshot is only ever returned for the one epoch this connection negotiated.

On a mismatch, the connection is terminated for renegotiation rather than continued: the client must call Negotiate again, which re-establishes a session, an epoch, and the capabilities/limits agreed for it as one combined negotiation outcome, and only then request another snapshot. The server never lets a client keep using capabilities or limits that were agreed for an epoch other than the one it is now operating under.

Build a complete, self-contained StageSnapshot rooted exactly at the negotiated bridge_root_path: every update needed to reconstruct the bridge-owned overlay from empty, never a diff against a prior snapshot

Bound the snapshot to MaxBridgeOverlayUpdates (4096) updates and MaxBridgeOverlayPayloadBytes (MaxEstimatedBatchPayloadBytes - 65536) estimated bytes; when authored Kit content would exceed either bound, the server must not silently truncate -- it fails the call rather than hand back a partial baseline the coordinator would misapply
Set sequence to the last remote sequence already covered by this snapshot's content, so a subsequent StageDelta at sequence + 1 continues without a gap
Treat the call as idempotent and safe to retry: identical inputs against an unchanged server state produce byte-identical output

preconditions: A prior successful Negotiate on this session
steps: Return a SessionStatus reflecting the server's own bounded counters at call time: state, epoch, last_accepted_sequence, last_applied_sequence, applied/duplicate/rejected/loop-suppressed counts, overlay size, and replay ledger occupancy

Track and report every one of SessionStatus's non-optional scalar fields (applied_snapshot_count, applied_delta_count, duplicate_delta_count, rejected_delta_count, loop_suppressed_delta_count, resync_required_count, overlay_prim_count, overlay_update_count, replay_window_length, replay_ledger_count, replay_ledger_bytes, oldest_retained_sequence, session_observer_failure_count) accurately. These are proto3 non-optional scalars with no wire-level absent state, so an unset value is indistinguishable from an accurately reported zero: the server never estimates one or reports a placeholder zero for one it does not actually track. A companion that cannot yet track one of these accurately has an implementation gap to close before claiming GetStatus support, or a case to raise as an optional field in a future protocol version; it is never omitted from the response, because it cannot be.

Redact last_failure_detail and last_session_observer_failure_detail exactly like the negotiated 'detail' fields: bounded length, never a credential, never raw payload bytes. Unlike the counters above, these two fields are proto3 optional and may legitimately be left unset when there is no failure to report.
Treat the call as read-only and safe to retry under a bounded transport retry policy

preconditions: A prior successful Negotiate that agreed CAPABILITY_LOCAL_EDIT_EXPORT
steps: Look up request.idempotency_key in the session's idempotency ledger before applying anything. On a fingerprint match, do not touch the stage a second time and do not return the ledger's original SESSION_OUTCOME_APPLIED Acknowledgement as if it were a fresh apply -- the ledger never stores that response. Instead form and return a new Acknowledgement with outcome SESSION_OUTCOME_DUPLICATE, sequence equal to the ledger entry's recorded sequence, correlation_id echoed from this request, and the session's current state -- see Idempotency key ledger for the exact rule.

On a miss, validate request.epoch against the current session epoch; reject SESSION_REJECTION_EPOCH_RETIRED for an old epoch and SESSION_REJECTION_EPOCH_ADVANCED for a newer one the server itself has not yet advertised. Either rejection means this connection's negotiated epoch is stale: the client must renegotiate (a fresh Negotiate call) rather than retry the same batch under the old epoch.
Validate request.sequence is the next expected per-epoch local sequence for this origin_id; reject SESSION_REJECTION_SEQUENCE_GAP on a skip -- the server never invents the missing sequence's content
Validate every update in request.updates targets a path at or under the negotiated bridge_root_path; reject SESSION_REJECTION_BRIDGE_SCOPE for any update outside it
Validate the resulting overlay would stay within MaxBridgeOverlayUpdates/MaxBridgeOverlayPayloadBytes; reject SESSION_REJECTION_OVERLAY_BUDGET otherwise

Canonicalize and re-validate every update against the checks above before issuing a single Kit-side authoring call; nothing is sent to the .live layer until every update in the batch has passed every check

Issue the Kit-side authoring calls for the batch against the bridge-owned .live layer, then record the idempotency-ledger entry and return SESSION_OUTCOME_APPLIED only after every one of those calls has completed successfully -- never before, and never merely after they were issued. This specification does not claim the batch commits as one atomic, rollback-safe transaction, and does not claim Nucleus persistence: no Kit API providing either guarantee has been evidenced. A companion that later adopts a Kit API with a genuinely evidenced atomic-replacement guarantee documents and evidences that separately; it is not assumed here.

On any partial or failed apply -- some authoring calls succeeded and a later one in the same batch failed -- return SESSION_REJECTION_APPLY_FAILED, stop emitting further StageDelta frames on this session's StreamChanges connection, send ResyncRequired, and let the next GetSnapshot rebuild the authoritative baseline from the Kit stage's actual current state rather than trying to reason about, or roll back, a partially-applied batch

Echo request.origin_id on the StageDelta this batch produces for every other subscriber on StreamChanges, so a subscriber whose own origin_id matches suppresses it as an echo instead of reapplying it; the publisher itself never receives its own batch back as a delta

Never retry a PublishLocalBatch at the transport layer; a mutating call is retried only by the client, only with the same idempotency_key, and only after a transport failure whose effect on the server is unknown

preconditions: The first ChangeStreamRequest frame on the stream carries a HandshakeRequest; every other request kind arriving first is rejected as SESSION_REJECTION_NOT_NEGOTIATED and the stream is closed
steps: After a successful embedded handshake, emit exactly one StageSnapshot before any StageDelta, at the epoch/sequence the handshake resolved

Every frame this connection sends or accepts after that carries exactly the negotiated session_id and epoch. If the server's authoritative epoch for this bridge root changes while the stream is open -- another Kit live session became authoritative, the live session was reset, or any other event that retires the negotiated epoch -- the server never switches this stream to the new epoch in place: it ends the stream (or answers the next frame with SESSION_REJECTION_EPOCH_ADVANCED / SESSION_REJECTION_EPOCH_RETIRED as appropriate) so the client renegotiates through a fresh Negotiate call, which re-establishes the epoch together with the capabilities and limits agreed for it, before any further snapshot or delta is exchanged.
Emit StageDelta frames in strictly increasing per-epoch sequence order for the one authoritative remote origin this session tracks; never interleave two origins' sequences into one numbering

Suppress delivering a delta back to the same connection that published it (echo suppression by origin_id), matching the client-side LoopSuppressed outcome so the coordinator on either side never double-applies its own edit

On detecting the server cannot maintain a gapless sequence for a subscriber -- a slow consumer, an internal buffer overrun, or a lost delta -- send ResyncRequired with the precise ResyncReason (RESYNC_REASON_SEQUENCE_GAP, RESYNC_REASON_SERVER_REQUESTED, etc.) rather than silently dropping or reordering deltas; do not close the stream to force this, resync happens in-band

Apply the negotiated effective_limits to backpressure: when the outbound direction cannot keep up with the server's own change rate, buffer up to a bounded, documented depth and then emit ResyncRequired rather than growing an unbounded queue or blocking the Kit main thread

Answer Acknowledgement, SnapshotRequest, PublishLocalBatchRequest, StatusRequest, and KeepAlive frames arriving on the same stream inline, in the order received, without reordering them relative to outbound deltas

On stream teardown (client disconnect, transport error, or server shutdown), release the session's negotiated capabilities/limits and idempotency ledger memory budget; a reconnect always re-negotiates rather than resuming a torn-down stream's in-memory state directly

During a clean server shutdown, stop accepting new Negotiate calls, allow in-flight PublishLocalBatch calls to finish, send a final SessionEvent/ResyncRequired as appropriate, and close existing streams so every connected client reconnects and resynchronizes against the next server instance rather than silently hanging

idempotencyLedger.keySource: PublishLocalBatchRequest.idempotency_key, an opaque bounded string the client derives from (session_id, epoch, sequence) when it does not supply its own; the server never derives or infers a key -- it only ever compares the one presented
rules: A ledger entry retains only a sequence and a bounded content fingerprint -- a hash over epoch, origin_id, correlation_id, coalescing_key, and updates -- never the full authored payload and never a stored copy of the original Acknowledgement, so retention cost does not grow with message size, mirroring OpenUsd.LiveAuthoring.LiveAuthoringValidation.ReplayLedgerEntryBytes

A replayed idempotency_key whose fingerprint matches the ledger entry (byte-identical epoch/origin_id/correlation_id/coalescing_key/updates) never re-applies and never returns the first, SESSION_OUTCOME_APPLIED Acknowledgement as if it were a fresh apply. The server forms and returns a new Acknowledgement with outcome SESSION_OUTCOME_DUPLICATE, sequence equal to the ledger entry's recorded sequence, correlation_id echoed from this replay request (necessarily identical to the original's, since the fingerprint matched), and the session's current state fields -- so a caller can never mistake a replay's answer for a second successful mutation, and the server never has to retain the first response to answer a replay

A reused idempotency_key whose fingerprint does not match the ledger entry -- its epoch, origin_id, correlation_id, coalescing_key, or updates differ -- is a DuplicateConflict: the server must reject it (SESSION_REJECTION_DUPLICATE_CONFLICT) and require a full resync rather than guess which version is authoritative

A key older than the bounded replay window (falls off the back of a size- or count-bounded ledger) can no longer be proven a duplicate; the server rejects it with SESSION_REJECTION_REPLAY_EXPIRED and requires a full resync instead of silently risking a double-apply
The ledger is bounded independently by both entry count (windowMaxLength) and byte size (maxLedgerBytes = windowMaxLength * entryBytes), never allowed to grow with session lifetime

updateMapping.notes: SetAttribute.time_code unset (SetAttributeUpdate.TimeCode == null) authors the attribute's default value; time_code set authors one discrete time sample at that code. Both are the same wire case -- there is no separate time-sample message.
Requires the CAPABILITY_API_SCHEMA capability to have been agreed during negotiation.
Requires the CAPABILITY_POINT_INSTANCER_ORIENTATIONS capability to have been agreed during negotiation.
Only representable as a StageSnapshot returned by GetSnapshot or pushed on StreamChanges. Encoding one inside a delta throws BridgeProtocolException(OverlayReplacementNotAllowed).

unsupportedEdits.kitEdit: Renaming or reparenting a prim inside the bridge-owned overlay
unsupportedEdits.reason: The wire model has no rename/move update case; RemovePrimUpdate plus DefinePrimUpdate at a new path would lose the identity continuity a rename implies, and could race with in-flight deltas that still reference the old path. The companion must send a full StageSnapshot instead.

unsupportedEdits.kitEdit: Sublayer, reference, or payload structure changes on the bridge root prim itself
unsupportedEdits.reason: As opposed to authoring SetReferenceUpdate/SetPayloadUpdate on a prim under the root: layer-structural edits change what composes the overlay, not a value inside it, and are outside the coordinator's single-prim-scoped update model. Requires a full snapshot.

unsupportedEdits.kitEdit: Restructuring variant sets (adding or removing a variant set or a variant)
unsupportedEdits.reason: As opposed to SetVariantSelectionUpdate choosing among existing variants: only variant selection is a wire case. Structural variant set changes require a full snapshot.

unsupportedEdits.kitEdit: A composition arc or override authored outside bridgeRootPath affecting prims inside it
unsupportedEdits.reason: The coordinator only accepts updates whose target path is at or under the bridge root; an edit reaching in from outside is bridge-scope-violating by construction and is never partially applied.

unsupportedEdits.kitEdit: Removing a single authored time sample in isolation
unsupportedEdits.reason: Leaving the default value and every other time sample intact: ClearUpdate's CLEAR_TARGET_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE clears an attribute's default value and all of its time samples together; there is no wire case for removing one discrete time sample without touching the rest. A companion needing that sends a full StageSnapshot instead.

unsupportedEdits.kitEdit: Any edit the server cannot express as a StageUpdate oneof case
unsupportedEdits.reason: The oneof is closed and versioned (see updateMapping for the full, cross-checked list); an update kind the current major version does not define is never approximated by a different case. It is deferred to a full snapshot and, if it recurs, to a proposed wire addition under a new minor version.

scoping.bridgeRootRule: Every StageUpdate the server sends or accepts targets a path at or under the one bridgeRootPath negotiated for the session. The server owns exactly one bridge root per negotiated session; a Kit stage that needs more than one independently-scoped overlay negotiates more than one session, each with its own SessionEpoch.
scoping.layerRule: The bridge-owned overlay is authored into the Kit-side .live layer the companion already owns; this repository's coordinator applies it to whatever layer the host process configured as the bridge overlay's edit target. Neither side reaches into a layer the other did not name for this purpose, and neither side restructures the *set* of layers as part of a bridge update -- see unsupportedEdits.
scoping.mergeRule: There is no general distributed merge. Exactly one remote origin is authoritative for a given session's ordered sequence; the server never combines edits from two different origins into one sequence position, and a client never guesses at a merge result. A Kit-side conflict between two Kit users is a live-session/Nucleus concern the companion resolves before it ever reaches this protocol -- by the time an edit reaches openusd.bridge.v1, it is already the one authoritative outcome for that origin.

headlessKitService.description: A non-interactive Kit process (no GUI extension loaded) that hosts only the openusd.bridge.v1 server and the Kit-side Nucleus/live-session machinery it depends on. Intended for a long-running bridge process co-located with, or reachable from, the process that hosts OpenUsd.Bridge.Grpc's client. Configuration -- listen address, TLS material, token validation -- is a companion-owned concern; this specification only fixes the wire contract and the loopback-by-default posture the C# client already assumes (docs/omniverse-bridge.md Security table).
healthEndpoints: GetStatus (unary RPC) is the primary health surface: a monitoring process negotiates once and polls GetStatus on a bounded interval

A process-level liveness probe (for example a container orchestrator's HTTP/TCP check) is a companion deployment concern outside openusd.bridge.v1 and is not specified here pending an authorized deployment target

guiExtension.description: An interactive Kit extension (omni.kit.uiapp-hosted) that additionally exposes the same server through a visible window: connection status, negotiated capabilities/limits, and the SessionStatus counters, using Kit's own extension.toml-declared UI dependencies. The server behavior in serverBehavior is identical in both modes; only the presence of a UI differs.
healthEndpoints: GetStatus (unary RPC), surfaced in the extension's own status window instead of (or in addition to) an external poller
SessionEvent frames on the open StreamChanges connection, surfaced as a live log/toast in the UI

logging: Every logged Acknowledgement, SessionEvent, or SessionStatus uses only the bounded 'detail' text already redacted by the protocol layer; the companion never logs a raw StageUpdate payload at a default log level, since authored scene data may be sensitive

Correlation identifiers (correlation_id) are propagated into the companion's own log lines so a single authored batch can be traced from the Kit-side capture through Negotiate/PublishLocalBatch/StreamChanges to the client-side receipt
metrics: SessionStatus's own counters (applied/duplicate/rejected/loop-suppressed delta counts, replay ledger occupancy, overlay size) are the specified metrics surface; a companion may additionally export them to its own metrics system, but must not invent counters this protocol does not define as the basis for a health claim
Backpressure and resync frequency (ResyncRequired counts by ResyncReason) are the specified signal for detecting a subscriber that cannot keep up
credentialRedaction: A presented token, header, or Nucleus credential is never included in a log line, a SessionEvent.detail, an Acknowledgement.detail, or a SessionStatus.last_failure_detail, mirroring BridgeCallCredential.ToString() printing '<redacted>' on the client side
A credential validation failure reports only that authentication failed (HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_UNAUTHENTICATED), never which part of the credential was wrong
Detail strings are length-bounded and never echo raw payload bytes, matching the client-side BridgeWireError contract

acceptanceMatrix.title: Round-trip authoring
acceptanceMatrix.method: A batch authored on the OpenUsd.LiveAuthoring side is published (PublishLocalBatch), observed as a StageDelta with the same origin_id on a second independently-negotiated connection, and re-applied there byte-for-byte equal to the source batch's updates.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: The second connection's applied overlay state is structurally equal to the first connection's local state, and the publishing connection never receives its own batch back as a non-echo-suppressed delta.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Session join and leave
acceptanceMatrix.method: A client negotiates, receives an initial StageSnapshot, disconnects cleanly (DisposeAsync-equivalent), and a second client negotiates fresh against the same server-owned bridge root.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: The leaving client's disposal is idempotent and presents no further credential or mutation; the joining client's snapshot reflects the full current overlay state with no residue from the first client's session identity or epoch.

acceptanceMatrix.title: 1000 ordered edits
acceptanceMatrix.method: 1000 sequentially numbered StageDelta or PublishLocalBatch updates are sent in strict per-epoch sequence order under the negotiated MaxUpdatesPerBatch/byte bounds.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: Every update is applied exactly once, in order, with no gap, no duplicate application, and the final overlay state matches the deterministic result of applying all 1000 updates in the sent order.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Time-sampled attribute authoring
acceptanceMatrix.method: A SetAttributeUpdate is published with SetAttribute.time_code set, authoring a discrete time sample rather than the default value; a second SetAttributeUpdate for the same attribute is published with time_code unset, authoring the default value; both are read back through GetSnapshot.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: The time-sampled write leaves the attribute's default value untouched and adds exactly one time sample at the given code; the default-value write does not add or remove any time sample; a snapshot faithfully separates the default value from every authored time sample rather than collapsing them.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Epoch change forces renegotiation, never silent adoption
acceptanceMatrix.method: While a client's StreamChanges connection is open, the server's authoritative epoch for the negotiated bridge root changes (for example a second Kit session takes over); separately, a client calls GetSnapshot with the request epoch it negotiated after the server's authoritative epoch has already advanced past it.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: The open connection never receives a Snapshot, Delta, or Acknowledgement frame naming the new epoch: it is terminated (or the next frame is rejected with SESSION_REJECTION_EPOCH_ADVANCED) so the client must call Negotiate again; GetSnapshot never substitutes a snapshot for a different epoch than the one requested -- it fails the call instead. In both cases the client only obtains the new epoch, its capabilities, and its limits together through a fresh Negotiate call, followed by a fresh GetSnapshot.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Reverse-order / out-of-order delivery
acceptanceMatrix.method: A transport redelivers a burst of already-sent sequences out of strict order (for example after a retransmit), including at least one sequence the receiver already applied.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: A sequence lower than the last accepted sequence is treated as SESSION_OUTCOME_DUPLICATE (identical content, answered with a freshly formed acknowledgement rather than the original SESSION_OUTCOME_APPLIED response) or SESSION_REJECTION_DUPLICATE_CONFLICT (differing content) per the idempotency ledger rules; the overlay is never mutated a second time by a re-delivered identical sequence, and a genuine conflict forces a full resync rather than an inconsistent partial apply.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Backpressure under a slow consumer
acceptanceMatrix.method: The server (or the client's bounded outbound queue, for local-edit export) is driven past its documented bounded buffer depth by a producer or change rate the consumer cannot keep up with.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: The bounded queue refuses admission (never grows unbounded) or the server emits ResyncRequired; no update is silently dropped without either an explicit rejection outcome or a resync request that lets the peer recover a consistent baseline.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Restart and full resync
acceptanceMatrix.method: The server process (or the client) is restarted mid-session, and the surviving peer reconnects.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: The reconnecting peer negotiates a new or resumed epoch, requests and applies a full StageSnapshot before accepting any StageDelta, and never applies a delta numbered against a stale, pre-restart epoch.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Authentication and protocol-version mismatch
acceptanceMatrix.method: A client presents an invalid or missing credential, and separately, a client whose major protocol version differs from the server's is negotiated against.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: An invalid/missing credential is rejected with HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_UNAUTHENTICATED before any capability or limit is evaluated; a major-version mismatch is rejected with HANDSHAKE_REJECTION_VERSION before capabilities or limits are evaluated; neither rejection ever attempts a mutation first.

acceptanceMatrix.title: Independent upgrade of client and server
acceptanceMatrix.method: The client is upgraded to a newer OpenUsd.Bridge.Protocol/Grpc minor version while the server stays on an older compatible minor version, and vice versa.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: Negotiation succeeds on major-version equality alone; the newer side's additional capabilities are simply absent from the agreed set when the older side does not advertise them, and no additional-capability update is sent or accepted by the side that does not support it.

acceptanceMatrix.title: License and dependency isolation
acceptanceMatrix.method: Building and testing this repository's OpenUsd.Bridge.Protocol/OpenUsd.Bridge.Grpc packages in isolation, without the companion repository present or referenced anywhere in this repository's source, build files, or restored packages.
acceptanceMatrix.passCriteria: Both packages restore, build, and test with no NVIDIA-licensed dependency, no reference to a companion repository, and no package manifest requiring one; tests/OpenUsd.Package.Tests/BridgePackageTests.cs continues to assert this, and this specification introduces nothing that would require it to change.
